---
title: The method
---

This page maps the equations of the method to the functions that implement them. The equation-level functions live in the submodules named below and are importable for teaching and testing; the pipeline functions `prepare_target`, `sweep_top_phi`, `run_drive`, `long_term_capacity` and `monte_carlo` chain them together, and `analyze` runs the whole chain.

## Overview

Each logged foot of driving is a load test of the soil at the pile toe. The method inverts the driving record in four steps:

1. Convert the blow count of each foot to a capacity at the time of driving with a recalibrated dynamic formula.
2. March down the pile. At each foot, subtract the shaft resistance of the feet above and find the friction angle whose toe bearing supplies the rest.
3. Treat every hammer blow as a cycle of shear on the soil near the toe. Count the blows each foot feels, compare them with the number that would liquefy it, and track the pore-pressure ratio $r_u$. Soil with elevated pore pressure carries less shaft resistance during driving and less toe bearing.
4. Sum the shaft resistance of every foot with its pore pressure dissipated and add the toe resistance at the end of the drive. That is the long-term capacity.

Stresses are in ksf, lengths in ft, forces in kips and angles in degrees.

## Capacity at the time of driving

The recalibrated Danish formula converts the set per blow $s = 1/\text{bpf}$ and the stroke $h$ into a capacity:

$$
Q = c_1 \frac{W h}{s + s_0} + c_2, \qquad
s_0 = \sqrt{\frac{W h L}{2 A E}}
$$

with ram weight $W$, pile length $L$, section area $A$ and modulus $E$. The Puget Sound recalibration of Reddy and Stuedlein (2013) gives $c_1 = 0.45$ and $c_2 = 0$.

| Quantity | Function |
|---|---|
| stroke from the blow rate, $h = \tfrac{g}{2}\left(\tfrac{30}{\text{bpm}}\right)^2$ | `bpm_to_stroke`, `stroke_to_bpm` |
| elastic set $s_0$ | `formulas.elastic_set` |
| capacity $Q$ per foot | `formulas.danish_capacity` |
| Savitzky-Golay smoothing of $Q$ over the log | `preprocess.smooth_capacity` |
| extension of the grid up to the mudline | `preprocess.extend_to_mudline` |
| static vertical effective stress $\sigma'_{v0}$ | `preprocess.sigma_v0_profile` |
| all of the above | `prepare_target` |

`prepare_target` returns a `Target`: the smoothed capacity, blow count, fines content and $\sigma'_{v0}$ of every foot on a one-foot grid from the mudline to the toe. The feet above the first logged foot are the unlogged top segment; their capacity is NaN.

## Toe bearing

The unit toe resistance is $q_p = N_q^* \sigma'_v$ with the Vesic (1977) cavity-expansion bearing factor

$$
N_q^* = \frac{1 + 2K_0}{3}\,
\frac{3}{3 - \sin\phi}\,
e^{(\pi/2 - \phi)\tan\phi}\,
\tan^2\!\left(45^\circ + \tfrac{\phi}{2}\right)
I_{rr}^{\,4\sin\phi / 3(1 + \sin\phi)}
$$

and $K_0 = 1 - \sin\phi$. The rigidity index comes from a stress-dependent small-strain shear modulus (Seed and Idriss, 1970) reduced to the strain level of bearing failure:

$$
I_r = \frac{(G/G_{max})\, G_{max}}{\sigma'_m \tan\phi}, \qquad
G_{max} = 21.7\, K_2\, p_a \sqrt{\sigma'_m / p_a}, \qquad
\sigma'_m = \frac{1 + 2K_0}{3}\sigma'_v
$$

$K_2$ is interpolated between its values at the friction-angle bounds and $I_r$ is clamped to `irr_bounds`.

| Quantity | Function |
|---|---|
| $N_q^*$ | `bearing.nq_vesic` |
| $I_r$ | `bearing.rigidity_index` |
| $q_p$ | `bearing.toe_bearing` |
| $\phi$ from a required $q_p$ (root find) | `bearing.phi_from_toe_bearing` |
| the same by interpolation on a grid | `bearing.phi_from_toe_bearing_grid` |

The inversion returns a reason code: `ok` when a friction angle inside `[phi_lo, phi_hi]` reproduces the required bearing, `below_floor` or `above_ceiling` when the requirement lies outside the attainable range and the angle is held at the bound, and `nonfinite` when the target is NaN.

## Friction angle and blow count

The friction angle is tied to the overburden-corrected blow count $N_{1,60}$ through the band midpoints of the WSDOT Geotechnical Design Manual (2022):

$$
\phi = \min\!\left(45^\circ,\; 26 + 5.5 \log_{10}(N_{1,60} + 0.01) + 0.11\, N_{1,60}\right)
$$

The march needs the inverse: the $N_{1,60}$ that the characterized $\phi$ implies, which feeds the liquefaction resistance and the residual strength. `ModelOptions.dphi` shifts the line; the Monte Carlo draws it.

| Quantity | Function |
|---|---|
| $\phi(N_{1,60})$ | `spt.phi_from_n160` |
| $N_{1,60}(\phi)$ | `spt.n160_from_phi` |

## Unliquefied shaft resistance

Coyle and Castello (1981) give the unit shaft resistance of a driven pile in sand as

$$
f_s = \sigma'_{v0}\, K_t(\phi)\, 10^{-0.017\, z / B} \tan\delta
$$

with depth $z$, pile width $B$ and interface friction angle $\delta = $ `cc_delta_ratio` $\times\,\phi$. $K_t$ is tabulated at 30, 33 and 36 degrees and extended above 36 degrees in proportion to the Nordlund coefficient at the pile's displaced volume.

| Quantity | Function |
|---|---|
| $K_t(\phi)$ | `shaft.coyle_castello_k` |
| Nordlund $K_\delta$ used for the extension | `shaft.nordlund_k_delta` |
| $f_s$ | `shaft.fs_coyle_castello` |

## Blows to liquefaction

A hammer blow that fails the soil at the toe applies a cyclic stress ratio

$$
\text{CSR} = \frac{\tau_{max}}{\sigma'_{v0}} = (1 - \sin\phi)\tan\phi
$$

The cyclic resistance ratio at the 15-cycle reference is the Boulanger and Idriss (2014) curve for the clean-sand equivalent blow count $N_{1,60cs} = N_{1,60} + \Delta N(FC)$, with the overburden factor $K_\sigma$. The number of uniform cycles that triggers liquefaction follows the cyclic strength curve of Idriss and Boulanger (2008):

$$
N_L = 15 \left(\frac{\text{CRR}_{15}}{\text{CSR}}\right)^{1/b}, \qquad b = 0.34
$$

| Quantity | Function |
|---|---|
| $\Delta N(FC)$ | `liquefaction.delta_n_fines` |
| $N_{1,60cs}$ | `liquefaction.n160_clean_sand` |
| $\text{CRR}_{M7.5}$ at 1 atm | `liquefaction.crr_m75` |
| $K_\sigma$ | `liquefaction.k_sigma` |
| $\text{CRR}_{15}$ in situ | `liquefaction.crr_15` |
| CSR | `liquefaction.csr_driving` |
| $N_L$ | `liquefaction.cycles_to_liquefaction` |
| all four for one foot | `march.triggering_state` |

## Pore-pressure ratio

The pore-pressure ratio of a foot grows linearly with the blows it has felt:

$$
r_u = \min\!\left(\frac{N_{felt}}{N_L},\; 1\right)
$$

A foot starts feeling blows when the toe is within `zone_factor` $\times B$ above it, and keeps feeling them until it liquefies or the drive ends. A liquefied foot no longer transmits blows to the feet above it.

| Quantity | Function |
|---|---|
| $r_u$ | `liquefaction.ru_linear` |
| blow accounting over the drive | `run_drive` |

## Residual strength

Liquefied soil retains the residual strength of Kramer and Wang (2015):

$$
S_r = p_a \exp\!\left(-8.444 + 0.109\, N_{1,60} + 5.379 \left(\sigma'_{v0}/p_a\right)^{0.1}\right)
$$

with $N_{1,60}$ capped at 15, the limit of the calibration.

| Quantity | Function |
|---|---|
| $S_r$ | `liquefaction.residual_strength` |

## Shaft resistance through partially liquefied soil

Between the unliquefied and liquefied states the unit shaft resistance is the larger of the reduced frictional resistance and the mobilized residual strength (Boulanger and Brandenberg, 2004):

$$
f_s(r_u) = \max\!\big((1 - r_u)\, f_s,\; r_u\, \alpha\, S_r\big)
$$

where $\alpha$ is the Randolph and Murphy (1985) interface factor on the undrained strength ratio $S_r / \sigma'_{v0}$.

| Quantity | Function |
|---|---|
| $\alpha$ | `shaft.interface_alpha` |
| $f_s(r_u)$ | `shaft.fs_partially_liquefied` |
| unit shaft resistance of a foot now and after dissipation | `march.fs_current`, `march.fs_unliquefied` |

## The march

`run_drive` walks the grid top down. At each logged foot it:

1. sums the shaft resistance of the feet above in their current state;
2. divides the remainder of the target capacity by the toe area to get the required unit toe resistance;
3. finds the friction angle that supplies it, together with the self-consistent pore-pressure ratio at the toe: the blows the foot has felt by the time the toe leaves it reduce the stress the toe bears on, which changes the friction angle, which changes $N_L$. The lowest root in `[0, ru_cap_toe]` is taken;
4. adds the foot's blows to every unliquefied foot within the felt zone and updates their $r_u$, marking the ones that reach $N_L$ as liquefied.

The feet of the unlogged top segment are assigned a constant friction angle `top_phi` and take part in the blow accounting like any other foot.

`sweep_top_phi` repeats the march for every `top_phi` from `phi_lo` to `phi_hi` in steps of `top_sweep_step` and records the root-mean-square misfit between the modeled and target capacities. The admissible band is the contiguous set of angles around the minimum whose misfit is within `max(top_sweep_tol_frac * rms_min, top_sweep_tol_kips)` of it. The deterministic analysis uses the lowest admissible angle.

## Long-term capacity

$$
Q_{LT} = P \sum_{\text{feet}} f_s^{\,unliq} \,\Delta z \;+\; A\, q_p^{\,EOD}
$$

The shaft term uses the unliquefied resistance of every foot, that is, the resistance after all excess pore pressure has dissipated. The toe term is the end-of-drive bearing of the final foot, on the stress reduced by its toe pore-pressure ratio, less the residual between the modeled and target capacities at that foot so that the end-of-drive total matches the log. No toe setup is modeled.

| Quantity | Function |
|---|---|
| shaft | `capacity.shaft_long_term` |
| toe | `capacity.toe_end_of_drive` |
| both, from a `DriveResult` | `long_term_capacity` |

## Monte Carlo

`monte_carlo` propagates five uncertainty sources through the march. Each realization draws:

| Source | Distribution | Option |
|---|---|---|
| bias of the capacity formula | lognormal, mean 1 | `bias_cov` |
| scatter of each foot's capacity about the smoothed target | normal, robust standard deviation of the raw-minus-smoothed residuals | `target_noise` |
| shift of the friction angle line | uniform on $\pm$ `dphi_bound` | `dphi_bound` |
| multiplier on the cyclic resistance ratio | lognormal, median 1 | `crr_sigma_ln` |
| top-segment friction angle | uniform over the admissible band | from `sweep_top_phi` |

Realizations are added in chunks until the 95 percent confidence half-width of the mean long-term capacity falls below `ci_target` of the mean, or `max_realizations` is reached. The result holds the per-realization capacities and draws and the per-foot friction angle percentiles.
